articles.title: Lanterns Fans Respond As HBO Max Shares "Should’ve Asked John’s Mom To Be The Green Lantern" Video
articles.summary: The article introduces a critical debate regarding John Stewart's parents' actions and motives concerning their son. It questions whether they are loving, dedicated individuals prioritizing his best interests, or if they are selfishly endangering him due to their own personal desires. The text sets up an ethical dilemma exploring their character and the potential impact on their child's well-being.

articles.title: India harnessing power of its industry for space programmes: Shah on EOS-05 launch
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated ISRO scientists for successfully launching India's first imaging satellite into geosynchronous orbit. This significant achievement marks a major advancement in the nation's space technology capabilities, enhancing India's observational prowess. The successful placement of this pioneering satellite is a testament to ISRO's expertise and commitment to national development.

articles.title: Correction: Holt-Laury as a gumball machine
articles.summary: This news details a correction to a scientific paper's citation. The second author's initials were incorrect for 'Holt-Laury as a gumball machine,' published in PLoS ONE. The accurate citation now identifies Vázquez-De Francisco, MJ as the correct author. This highlights the vital importance of precision in academic referencing and maintaining research integrity.

articles.title: LANTERNS Producer Calls the Green Lantern Ring "Sexist" and Reveals Some Writers Knew Nothing About the Character
articles.summary: The article highlights Hal Jordan, a DCU character, who has become a significant target of criticism since 'Lanterns' premiered. Accusations of racism have been leveled against him, and even his iconic Green Lantern ring is reportedly facing scrutiny. This ongoing controversy underscores the negative reception and narrative challenges surrounding the character within the DC Universe.

articles.title: In 1974, President Ronald Reagan bought the 688-acre Rancho del Cielo near Santa Barbara; sold 24 years later, it became a California State Landmark in 2002
articles.summary: Former US President Ronald Reagan purchased the expansive 688-acre Rancho del Cielo near Santa Barbara in 1974. This significant property, serving as his 'Western White House', was later sold after 24 years. It subsequently transitioned into a California State property, preserving a piece of presidential history and the state's natural heritage.

articles.title: In 2003, New Jersey opened a 42-foot bridge made from discarded milk jugs and cups; the plastic span can carry a fully loaded 36,000-pound fire truck
articles.summary: In 2003, New Jersey unveiled a groundbreaking 42-foot bridge constructed entirely from discarded plastic, specifically milk jugs and cups. This innovative span showcases the incredible potential of recycled materials, demonstrating its robust engineering by successfully supporting a fully loaded 36,000-pound fire truck. It stands as an early example of sustainable infrastructure capable of handling significant loads, merging environmental responsibility with practical application.

articles.title: Australia eyes space-sector tie-ups in India; 3-5 deals likely next week
articles.summary: Australia is actively seeking deeper commercial space cooperation with India, identifying key opportunities in earth observation, satellite manufacturing, launch services, and space biotechnology. This initiative aims to strengthen bilateral ties and leverage each nation's expertise in the rapidly expanding space sector, fostering mutual growth and technological advancement between the two countries.

articles.title: Karnataka CM to lead all-party delegation to PM Modi for farm loan waiver amid drought
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced plans to lead an all-party delegation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The delegation aims to seek a waiver for farm loans in Karnataka. This critical step is being taken due to severe drought conditions devastating the state's agricultural sector, highlighting state-centre coordination for farmer relief and disaster management amidst economic distress.
